title: A Wardrobe for the Weather
premise: Sable Brightwater has spent eleven years mailing postcards to the house where her sister Dovie died in a fire the town called an accident — postcards no one answers, confessions she can't say aloud. When that house is scheduled for auction, Sable returns to the small coastal town of Merrow's Point and discovers the fire was set to cover up what Dovie knew about the town's beloved patriarch, Judge Alden Voss. As the auction approaches, Sable must choose between protecting the family who sheltered her afterward and telling the truth that will burn them all. She testifies at the auction's final hour, loses the house, but gains the goodbye she owed — speaking Dovie's name into the record as the gavel falls.
about_author: L. M. Eriksen is the pen name of a former court stenographer from the Pacific Northwest who spent two decades transcribing other people's truths before writing her own. Her fiction is known for quiet sentences that carry heavy weather, and for characters who mistake silence for safety.

chapters.title: The Smile That Ends Conversations
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. In her city life, we see her ritual: buying postcards of lighthouses, writing to a burned address, never sending return information. A coworker's casual kindness nearly cracks her open, and she deploys the smile. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as composure; establish the wound without naming it.

chapters.title: Notice of Sale
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A legal notice arrives by mistake — the Brightwater house goes to auction in thirty days. Sable takes leave from work and drives to Merrow's Point, telling herself it's about paperwork. She stands in the overgrown yard and hears, for the first time in years, someone say Dovie's name out loud. Beat: dread braided with longing.

chapters.title: What the Neighbors Kept
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Ruthie Calloway, Sable's childhood friend, now the town librarian. Ruthie is warm but guarded, and lets slip that people still talk about 'that night.' Sable learns the Voss family bought half the street after the fire. Beat: the past is not past; suspicion begins its slow work.

chapters.title: A Wardrobe for the Weather
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, flashback woven through present. Sorting the house's surviving boxes, Sable finds Dovie's coat and, sewn into the lining, a page torn from a ledger — numbers, dates, the judge's initials. Memory floods back: Dovie worked summers at the Voss estate. Beat: grief becomes evidence; the mystery turns personal.

chapters.title: The Judge's Open Door
chapters.summary: Judge Alden Voss's POV. Charming, aging, revered, he receives Sable graciously and offers to buy her silence along with the house — generously. He speaks of Dovie with unsettling tenderness. Sable leaves shaken, unsure whether he confessed or threatened. Beat: power wears a kind face; reader sees his corruption from inside.

chapters.title: Loyalty Is a Small Town
chapters.summary: Ruthie's POV. Ruthie warns Sable that the Calloways owe the Vosses everything — including Ruthie's job and her brother's acquittal years ago. She begs Sable to let the auction pass quietly. Their friendship fractures. Beat: loyalty vs. truth made intimate; Sable stands alone by choice.

chapters.title: Eleven Years of Postcards
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Confronted by the retired postal clerk who kept returning her unsent mail, Sable finally reads the stack aloud in the empty house — every confession, every apology to Dovie. She realizes the letters were never to Dovie; they were testimony waiting for a courtroom. Beat: catharsis; resolve hardens into purpose.

chapters.title: The Ledger Page
chapters.summary: Ruthie's POV. Ruthie, unable to live with her silence, cross-references the ledger fragment against library archives: payments matching the year three Voss employees 'moved away,' including the fire inspector who ruled Dovie's death accidental. She brings it to Sable at midnight. Beat: alliance reborn; the machinery of justice outside the law begins turning.

chapters.title: Going Once
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converge. Auction day: the courthouse lawn crowded, Voss's attorney bidding, and Sable taking the microphone during public comment to read the ledger page and name the inspector. Chaos; the auction halts; the state attorney general's office, tipped by Ruthie, is already in the crowd. Beat: climax — truth spoken aloud at last, at maximum cost.

chapters.title: Out Loud
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, weeks later. The house sells to a young family; Voss resigns under investigation; Ruthie keeps her job and her honesty. Sable mails one final postcard — to herself, at her own address — saying goodbye properly. Standing in the yard, she says Dovie's name to the open sky. Beat: resolution; grief given weather, voice, and release.
